questions.question: What is a processed food? Give two examples and one good thing about processing.
questions.expected_answer: A processed food has been changed from its natural form, for example by drying, grinding, cooking, tinning, freezing or adding ingredients. Examples are maize meal, biltong, jam, chips, polony and tinned beans. Processing makes food last longer and can make it safer, like pasteurised milk, or more nutritious, like fortified maize meal.

questions.question: Name five things that are often added to processed foods and say why each is added.
questions.expected_answer: Salt is added for taste and to help food last. Sugar is added for sweetness. Preservatives stop food going bad too quickly. Flavourings give food a certain taste. Colourings make food look attractive.

questions.question: Why should we eat foods with lots of added salt and sugar only in small amounts? How can a label help?
questions.expected_answer: Too much salt over many years can cause high blood pressure, and too much sugar can cause tooth decay, being overweight and diabetes. Such foods often have little fibre and few vitamins. The label lists ingredients from the biggest amount to the smallest, so if salt or sugar is near the top, the food contains a lot of it.
